speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I understand you are experiencing right groin pain and have an abnormal leg positioning after a rear-end collision. To properly assess your injury, can you tell me exactly how your leg is positioned when you are sitting or standing?

speaker: Patient
text: 25-year-old female. The patient was involved in a rear-end collision where she was the restrained driver of the back car. She reports immediate onset of pain in both knees and severe pain over the right groin area following the accident.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that detail. Given the rear-end collision mechanism and immediate onset of pain in both knees along with severe right groin pain, I need to clarify the nature of your leg deformity. When you mention "abnormal positioning," does the right leg appear externally rotated (turned outward) or internally rotated (turned inward)? Additionally, have you noticed any bruising or swelling developing in the groin or thigh since the accident?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Severe right groin pain. I also have Pain in both knees, Right leg is slightly shortened, flexed, adducted, and internally rotated.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Right Femoral Neck Fracture. The mechanism of injury (rear-end collision) combined with the classic presentation of a shortened, flexed, adducted, and internally rotated leg confirms this diagnosis. I will not request further tests as the clinical picture is definitive.
